subject: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 spike + timeouts — suspected KV-cache / batching issue
messages:

Cc: SaaS Ops <ops@lattice-systems.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike across inference routes

Evelyn —

We're seeing a sustained spike in 5xx and 429 for most of our customer-facing routes starting ~08:45 PDT. End users are getting 504s and retries are piling up on our side, which is compounding the problem. We pushed a configuration change to increase client retries (per your suggestion) two weeks ago; that might be making the retry storm worse.

Key metrics (last 30m):
- 5xx rate: 6.1% (baseline ~0.02%)
- 429 rate: 3.4%
- median latency: 1.2s -> 6.8s
- p95 latency: 3.6s -> 22s
- spikes of queue length on the routing layer, CPU on s-infer-03 at 92%

Can you confirm what's happening on your side? This is impacting our checkout flow.

Thanks,
Alex Rowan
Sr. SRE, Lattice Systems

Alex — thanks for flagging this. I'm escalating internally now and we'll provide a mitigation plan within 30 minutes.

Initial ask: can you share a representative request id (or two) that's returned 504 and the approximate timestamps? That will help us correlate traces.

Mitigation steps we're spinning up immediately:
- Disable batching for your tenant on the inference layer (temporary)
- Push a fallback routing policy to divert to a smaller-capacity pool with higher timeouts
- Throttle client-side retries via a short-lived client config we can push to you (if you accept)

Diego, Marcus, Monica — I'm assigning this as P0 for Lattice. Please coordinate and keep me updated in-thread. I'll loop in leadership if we need credits/SLA concessions.

Evelyn Hart

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:36:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike across inference routes

Working the trace correlation now. Early findings from tail logs: repeated KV-cache evictions and misses for a small set of keys tied to the streaming prefix cache. There's a pattern of hot prefixes that blow out the cache and cause synchronous fetches -> queueing on the request processing goroutine pool. Combined with longer client retries this looks like a classic retry-amplified queueing event.

Concrete actions I'm proposing (immediate):
1) Disable prefix/KV caching only for Lattice for the next 30 minutes to eliminate thrash.
2) Temporarily set batching_size=1 for their routes (effectively disabling batching) — this reduces blocking behind long tail microbatches.
3) Increase request handler pool for s-infer-01..04 by 50% (hotfix) so queued requests can drain.
4) Force circuit-breaker to open earlier (lower concurrency threshold) for their tenant to avoid cascading failures.

I'm pushing a patch to the routing config now. Will attach logs.

- Diego
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 5xx/429 spike across inference routes

Quick update: I applied steps 1 and 2 (disabled KV cache + batching_size=1) for Lattice. Early telemetry (10 minutes after change):
- 5xx rate down to 0.9%
- 429 rate down to 0.5%
- median latency back to ~1.4s
- p95 now ~4.1s (still improving)

We still see elevated CPU on s-infer-03 but queue lengths are dropping. I'll keep monitoring.

We need a postmortem plan: recommended RCA hypothesis — batching + prefix cache thrash + increased retries = synchronous stalls and queueing leading to timeouts. We should consider a long-term fix in the runtime: per-tenant cache admission and better backpressure on batching.

Marcus Lin
Software Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
